title.narrative: Integrated Hunger Gap Project for Most Vulnerable Populations in Malakal PoC, Malakal North and Mala

description.narrative:
This project targets Malakal County, which is part of Upper Nile State. An estimated 6,115 household have been camping at Malakal POC (Population: M = 16,714 F = 17,682) ) People in the POCs have completely been depending on relief foods from WFP, while FAO and other organizations have been implementing FSL and peace building interventions in Malakal and its nearby Counties/Payams. However, enormous humanitarian needs remain unfulfilled since IDPs in POCs sites receive insufficient relief food. Already, WFP has declared its intention to scale down the food supplies, due to funding gaps; spelling more danger to people dependent on WFP blanket food distributions.
In an attempt to assuage the situation in Malakal County, ADA, through a running CAFOD-funding project has targeted 800 HH with agricultural inputs (seeds, tools and fishing gear). The inputs are meant to increase agricultural production in households and boost household fishing, for both food and sale. While this would help the beneficiaries to improve household security, the current food crisis in the area creates serious hunger in beneficiary households.
With the foregoing in view, this project intends to complement the current efforts by WFP, FAO and ADA/CAFOD in providing food in kind supplies to the people of Malakal PoC, Malakal North and Malakal South. The net effect is to provide needed household daily feeding support to farmers as they cultivate and wait for the harvests.
